    61→def wrap_sync_to_async_unsafe(func: Callable[..., Any]) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    62→    """Wrap a callable in a coroutine that executes the callable directly.
    63→
    64→    This helper makes it easier to use synchronous callables with ASGI
    65→    apps. However, it is considered "unsafe" because it calls the wrapped
    66→    function directly in the same thread as the asyncio loop. Generally, you
    67→    should use :func:`~.wrap_sync_to_async` instead.
    68→
    69→    Warning:
    70→        This helper is only to be used for functions that do not perform any
    71→        blocking I/O or lengthy CPU-bound operations, since the entire async
    72→        loop will be blocked while the wrapped function is executed.
    73→        For a safer, non-blocking alternative that runs the function in a
    74→        thread pool executor, use :func:`~.sync_to_async` instead.
    75→
    76→    Arguments:
    77→        func (callable): Function, method, or other callable to wrap
    78→
    79→    Returns:
    80→        function: An awaitable coroutine function that wraps the
    81→        synchronous callable.
    82→    """
    83→
    84→    @wraps(func)
    85→    async def wrapper(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    86→        return func(*args, **kwargs)
    87→
    88→    return wrapper

    91→def wrap_sync_to_async(
    92→    func: Callable[..., Any], threadsafe: Optional[bool] = None
    93→) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    94→    """Wrap a callable in a coroutine that executes the callable in the background.
    95→
    96→    This helper makes it easier to call functions that can not be
    97→    ported to use async natively (e.g., functions exported by a database
    98→    library that does not yet support asyncio).
    99→
   100→    To execute blocking operations safely, without stalling the async
   101→    loop, the wrapped callable is scheduled to run in the background, on a
   102→    separate thread, when the wrapper is called.
   103→
   104→    Normally, the default executor for the running loop is used to schedule the
   105→    synchronous callable. If the callable is not thread-safe, it can be
   106→    scheduled serially in a global single-threaded executor.
   107→
   108→    Warning:
   109→        Wrapping a synchronous function safely adds a fair amount of overhead
   110→        to the function call, and should only be used when a native async
   111→        library is not available for the operation you wish to perform.
   112→
   113→    Arguments:
   114→        func (callable): Function, method, or other callable to wrap
   115→
   116→    Keyword Arguments:
   117→        threadsafe (bool): Set to ``False`` when the callable is not
   118→            thread-safe (default ``True``). When this argument is ``False``,
   119→            the wrapped callable will be scheduled to run serially in a
   120→            global single-threaded executor.
   121→
   122→    Returns:
   123→        function: An awaitable coroutine function that wraps the
   124→        synchronous callable.
   125→    """
   126→
   127→    if threadsafe is None or threadsafe:
   128→        executor = None  # Use default
   129→    else:
   130→        executor = _one_thread_to_rule_them_all
   131→
   132→    @wraps(func)
   133→    async def wrapper(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
   134→        return await get_running_loop().run_in_executor(
   135→            executor, partial(func, *args, **kwargs)
   136→        )
   137→
   138→    return wrapper

   142→    func: Callable[..., Any], *args: Any, **kwargs: Any
   143→) -> Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]]:
   144→    """Schedule a synchronous callable on the default executor and await the result.
   145→
   146→    This helper makes it easier to call functions that can not be
   147→    ported to use async natively (e.g., functions exported by a database
   148→    library that does not yet support asyncio).
   149→
   150→    To execute blocking operations safely, without stalling the async
   151→    loop, the wrapped callable is scheduled to run in the background, on a
   152→    separate thread, when the wrapper is called.
   153→
   154→    The default executor for the running loop is used to schedule the
   155→    synchronous callable.
   156→
   157→    Warning:
   158→        This helper can only be used to execute thread-safe callables. If
   159→        the callable is not thread-safe, it can be executed serially
   160→        by first wrapping it with :func:`~.wrap_sync_to_async`, and then
   161→        executing the wrapper directly.
   162→
   163→    Warning:
   164→        Calling a synchronous function safely from an asyncio event loop
   165→        adds a fair amount of overhead to the function call, and should
   166→        only be used when a native async library is not available for the
   167→        operation you wish to perform.
   168→
   169→    Arguments:
   170→        func (callable): Function, method, or other callable to wrap
   171→        *args: All additional arguments are passed through to the callable.
   172→
   173→    Keyword Arguments:
   174→        **kwargs: All keyword arguments are passed through to the callable.
   175→
   176→    Returns:
   177→        function: An awaitable coroutine function that wraps the
   178→        synchronous callable.
   179→    """
   180→

   182→        None, partial(func, *args, **kwargs)

   194→def _wrap_non_coroutine_unsafe(
   195→    func: Optional[Callable[..., Any]],
   196→) -> Union[Callable[..., Awaitable[Any]], Callable[..., Any], None]:
   197→    """Wrap a coroutine using ``wrap_sync_to_async_unsafe()`` for internal test cases.
   198→
   199→    This method is intended for Falcon's own test suite and should not be
   200→    used by apps themselves. It provides a convenient way to reuse sync
   201→    methods for ASGI test cases when it is safe to do so.
   202→
   203→    Arguments:
   204→        func (callable): Function, method, or other callable to wrap
   205→    Returns:
   206→        When not in test mode, this function simply returns the callable
   207→        unchanged. Otherwise, if the callable is not a coroutine function,
   208→        it will be wrapped using ``wrap_sync_to_async_unsafe()``.
   209→    """
   210→
   211→    if func is None:
   212→        return func
   213→
   214→    if not _should_wrap_non_coroutines():
   215→        return func
   216→
   217→    if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(func):
   218→        return func
   219→
   220→    return wrap_sync_to_async_unsafe(func)

   223→def async_to_sync(
   224→    coroutine: Callable[..., Awaitable[Result]], *args: Any, **kwargs: Any
   225→) -> Result:
   226→    """Invoke a coroutine function from a synchronous caller.
   227→
   228→    This method can be used to invoke an asynchronous task from a synchronous
   229→    context. The coroutine will be scheduled to run on the current event
   230→    loop for the current OS thread. If an event loop is not already running,
   231→    one will be created.
   232→
   233→    Warning:
   234→        Executing async code in this manner is inefficient since it involves
   235→        synchronization via threading primitives, and is intended primarily for
   236→        testing, prototyping or compatibility purposes.
   237→
   238→    Note:
   239→        On Python 3.11+, this function leverages a module-wide
   240→        ``asyncio.Runner``.
   241→
   242→    Args:
   243→        coroutine: A coroutine function to invoke.
   244→        *args: Additional args are passed through to the coroutine function.
   245→
   246→    Keyword Args:
   247→        **kwargs: Additional args are passed through to the coroutine function.
   248→    """
   249→    return _active_runner().run(coroutine(*args, **kwargs))
   250→

   252→def runs_sync(coroutine: Callable[..., Awaitable[Result]]) -> Callable[..., Result]:
   253→    """Transform a coroutine function into a synchronous method.
   254→
   255→    This is achieved by always invoking the decorated coroutine function via
   256→    :meth:`async_to_sync`.
   257→
   258→    Warning:
   259→        This decorator is very inefficient and should only be used for adapting
   260→        asynchronous test functions for use with synchronous test runners such
   261→        as ``pytest`` or the ``unittest`` module.
   262→
   263→        It will create an event loop for the current thread if one is not
   264→        already running.
   265→
   266→    Args:
   267→        coroutine: A coroutine function to masquerade as a synchronous one.
   268→
   269→    Returns:
   270→        callable: A synchronous function.
   271→    """
   272→
   273→    @wraps(coroutine)
   274→    def invoke(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
   275→        return async_to_sync(coroutine, *args, **kwargs)
   276→
   277→    return invoke

    21→from typing import Any, Callable, Optional

    32→class AttributeRemovedError(AttributeError):
    33→    """A deprecated attribute, class, or function has been subsequently removed."""
    34→
    35→
    36→# NOTE(kgriffs): We don't want our deprecations to be ignored by default,
    37→# so create our own type.

    39→# TODO(kgriffs): Revisit this decision if users complain.
    40→class DeprecatedWarning(UserWarning):

    44→def deprecated(
    45→    instructions: str, is_property: bool = False, method_name: Optional[str] = None
    46→) -> Callable[[Callable[..., Any]], Any]:
    47→    """Flag a method as deprecated.
    48→
    49→    This function returns a decorator which can be used to mark deprecated
    50→    functions. Applying this decorator will result in a warning being
    51→    emitted when the function is used.
    52→
    53→    Args:
    54→        instructions (str): Specific guidance for the developer, e.g.:
    55→            'Please migrate to add_proxy(...)'.
    56→        is_property (bool): If the deprecated object is a property. It
    57→            will omit the ``(...)`` from the generated documentation.
    58→        method_name (str, optional): Set to override the name of the
    59→            deprecated function or property in the generated
    60→            documentation (default ``None``). This is useful when
    61→            decorating an alias that carries the target's ``__name__``.
    62→
    63→    """
    64→
    65→    def decorator(func: Callable[..., Any]) -> Callable[[Callable[..., Any]], Any]:
    66→        object_name = 'property' if is_property else 'function'
    67→        post_name = '' if is_property else '(...)'
    68→        message = 'Call to deprecated {} {}{}. {}'.format(
    69→            object_name, method_name or func.__name__, post_name, instructions
    70→        )
    71→
    72→        @functools.wraps(func)
    73→        def wrapper(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    74→            warnings.warn(message, category=DeprecatedWarning, stacklevel=2)
    75→
    76→            return func(*args, **kwargs)
    77→
    78→        return wrapper
    79→
    80→    return decorator
